title: SLI orchestration and trace budget playbook for analytics pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement an orchestration layer and operational playbook that maps analytics pipeline SLIs to dynamic trace budgets and sampling policies so we can (1) detect regressions earlier, (2) limit trace costs adaptively, and (3) provide clear runbooks and dashboards for incident responders.

Motivation: Our current tracing and SLI collection for analytics ingest and Console pipelines is static and either under-captures important tail behavior or explodes cost during tenant spikes. This ticket scopes a pragmatic controller and playbook that ties observable signal quality (trace fullness, KV-cache miss rates, batch tail latency) to short-lived sampling amplifications and to synthetic probe triggers. The goal is to maintain SLOs while bounding trace/storage budget across tenants and features.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI -> trace-budget mapping document exists and is reviewed by PM/Platform (latency P50/P95, ingestion success rate, per-tenant error rate).
A controller prototype that adjusts trace sampling rates based on cost budget and recent SLI degradation is running in staging and tied to a feature flag.
Dashboards: per-tenant trace budget consumption, sampling rate, SLI deltas (30m/1h), and cost forecast available in Console.
Automated alerts that combine SLI breaches and abnormal trace-budget burn are in place with playbook links.
Runbook: step-by-step incident flow for an analytics SLI regression including safe rollback, temporary trace amplification, and post-incident cost reconciliation.
Integration tests: synthetic probes that validate controller behavior for three failure modes (ingest backpressure, KV-cache spike, batching degradation).
updates: 2026-02-10 Asha Patel: Drafted ticket. Initial scope focuses on controller + dashboards + runbook. Recommended prototype before wide rollout.

2026-02-16 Miguel Alvarez: Spike complete: evaluated reservoir vs. probabilistic adaptive sampling. Chosen approach: hybrid reservoir for tail spans + probability-based head sampling to keep per-tenant budgets stable.
2026-02-22 Engineering sync: Agreed to use existing trace-ingest topic and extend it with a "trace_budget" header to avoid schema churn. Need small tracing client change (PR linked).
2026-02-28 Design review: Dashboard mockups validated by Observability PM. Added per-route SLI breakdown and a burn-rate forecast widget. Action: add alert escalation for sustained 3x burn-rate.

2026-03-05 Miguel Alvarez: Prototype deployed to staging behind feature flag. Controller reduces sampling to preserve budget and temporarily amplifies sampling for journeys where synthetic probes fail. Observed 23% reduction in storage cost in staging traffic window.
2026-03-10 Security review: No PII changes; tracing retention policy will be enforced by retention controller. Security approved as low risk.
2026-03-12 Asha Patel: Preparing RFC for rollout plan and cost guardrails. Next steps: end-to-end load test and canary on low-risk tenant cohort.
risks: Over-aggressive sampling reduction could hide root-cause signals leading to longer MTTR.
Per-tenant budget enforcement may create noisy neighbor alerts if burst allowances are too strict.
Complexity in correlating batched requests to spans when sampling rates shift rapidly; might require trace rehydration heuristics.
Cost model drift: forecast may underpredict storage costs for models that emit larger spans (e.g., long KV caches).
technical_notes: Controller design: PID-like smoother that adjusts sampling_rate = clamp(base_rate * (1 + alpha * slo_delta), min_rate, max_rate).
Sampling strategy: head (first N spans per request) uses fixed probability sampling; tail spans use a reservoir with priority sampling to capture rare slow paths.
Integration: emit a lightweight "trace_budget" metric to metrics pipeline every 1m per-tenant. Budget reconciler runs every 5m and persists state in PartitionedKV for HA.
Retention: cheap traces (<1KB) retained 7d for on-call debugging; full traces retained per-tenant up to budget or 30d with approvals. This is enforced by retention-controller service.
Telemetry: add a synthetic probe that injects a trace with deterministic span names to validate sampling and retention paths end-to-end.
next_steps: Finish integration tests for the three failure modes and add load-test ramp to staging (Miguel).
Finalize dashboard panels and alert thresholds with Observability PM (Asha).
Rollout plan: canary to 5% of tenants for 48h then 25% then 100% with automated rollback on critical SLI breach (engineering + SRE).
